q2_gaps: A collective head noun premodified by a noun naming its member kind, written as a compound ('the nightmoth crowd') — Compound concepts would fuse it (nightmoth_crowd + genus crowd) while Coordination & plurals' collective-noun rule ('a flock of birds' → Member + GroupOf) is stated only for the of-phrase form; nothing adjudicates which route the compound form takes.
notes: Patient for the intransitive 'recovers' (internal change of state), the bare simple present with no status atom, the solid-spelling genus (Inheritance nightmoth moth) with the noun modifier 'night' left unexposed, and the no-distribution-rule treatment of the singular collective 'crowd' all follow the instruction set. The GroupOf route taken here is the semantically better of the two unadjudicated options.
